title: revenexx App Billing
description: Marketplace billing declaration for a revenexx App. Defines how the app is priced and distributed. Without billing.json, the app is private to the vendor. Required for App Marketplace distribution. NOTE: Billing model is an open decision — this schema is a first PoC implementation.

oneOf.title: A paid package names its price
A free or included package does not have to

$schema.description: Reference to this JSON Schema for editor validation and autocompletion.

type.description: 'free' — available at no cost in the Marketplace. 'paid' — requires a subscription plan (processed via Chargebee). 'included' — bundled with the Customer's billing package (no separate charge, activated by Console based on package).

support.description: Support contact information displayed in the Marketplace and Cockpit.

price.description: What this package costs per month, in one currency. Required when type is 'paid'. ONE package, ONE price: there are no tiers to choose between, so there is nothing to name them. The YEARLY price is deliberately not declared here — it is twelve monthly ones less 20%, derived by the platform, because a discount a vendor can write down is a discount a vendor can undercut. The revenue split is not here either: it is the same for every partner and is not something a package states about itself.

monthly.description: Price per month, charged to the tenant that installs this package.

trial.description: Optional trial period before billing starts.

legal.description: What a customer has to be able to read BEFORE installing, and what the platform has to be able to check before listing. Every field is a URL a person can open without an account — a policy behind a login is not a policy the buyer can read. All of them are optional HERE on purpose: a `required` in this schema would act on every package already registered, so none could ship even a hotfix until it had one. Which of these blocks a release is the release gate's decision, and it is applied in stages.

privacy_policy.description: What this package collects, what it does with it, how long it keeps it and how it is deleted. Reachable without a login.

terms.description: What the customer accepts by installing this package.

dpa.description: The data processing agreement — where, and on whose behalf, personal data is processed.

subprocessors.description: Who else sees data this package sends out of the platform. The hosts here are the ones the manifest already declares as `permissions.outbound` grants — that register says WHERE data goes, and default-denies the rest; this says WHY and under which agreement, which a grant cannot express. The two are joined by the host name, so a recipient named here and not granted there is a contradiction worth catching.

host.description: The hostname data is sent to, as the manifest's outbound grant spells it (e.g. 'api.stripe.com').

purpose.description: Why this recipient receives it, in words a customer reads on the product page.

dpa.description: This recipient's own data processing agreement, where it has one of its own.

available_countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes where this app is available. Omit or use ['*'] for all countries.

localizableText.description: Marketplace-facing text. Either a plain string — which the Marketplace shows in every UI language — or a map of BCP-47 language tag to text. 'en' is required and is the fallback whenever the reader's locale has no entry, so a half-translated listing degrades to English rather than to a blank. Every entry must hold at least one non-blank character. The plain string stays valid forever; no existing billing.json has to be converted.

listing.description: Optional rich Marketplace listing for the app's product page (VTEX-style). All fields optional → backward-compatible. Pricing (type/plans/trial), support and categories come from the billing root above; this block holds the marketing/discovery content. NOTE: `rating` is author-declared today and platform-aggregated later. Reviews are not declared here at all — they are real customer reviews the platform holds, so a manifest cannot seed them.

media.description: Screenshots, video and gallery imagery for the listing. Every reference here is either an absolute URL — an asset already hosted somewhere — or a path relative to the app root (e.g. "media/screenshot-catalog.png"), which the build uploads to the platform CDN and rewrites to its URL, exactly as `manifest.json#icon` works. Shipping the file in the repo is the shorter road and the one that keeps working: a URL to a host the app does not own outlives the file behind it.

screenshots.description: Screenshots shown in the gallery. An absolute URL, or a repo-relative path the build hosts for you. PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or SVG.

video.description: Optional demo/overview video. An absolute URL, or a repo-relative path the build hosts for you. MP4 or WebM.

gallery.description: Additional gallery imagery beside the screenshots. An absolute URL, or a repo-relative path the build hosts for you. PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF or SVG.

highlights.description: Short bullet highlights for the listing header.

scopes.description: What the app can access — drives the consent screen.

reason.description: Why the app needs it (shown on the consent screen).

verified.description: Whether the publisher is verified by revenexx.
